cue: Wave one hand side to side (Hello / Hi)
description: The robot raises its arm to a visible waving position, then performs a repetitive, friendly side-to-side motion with its gripper, resembling a human wave.
The robot lifts one arm into a clear acknowledgement pose, gives a small visible accent at the top, and settles slightly while preserving the greeting read.

cue: Bring one hand to forehead in salute position (Salute)
description: The robot moves its gripper to the forehead region with a vertical orientation, then adds a smaller coupled elbow movement to create a crisp in-between salute angle, holding that final silhouette long enough for the salute to read clearly.
The robot raises its arm toward the side of its head, settles the gripper near the temple region, traces small circles there, and eases out while preserving the 'crazy' read.
The robot moves its hand deliberately to one eye, performs a gentle rubbing motion to convey tiredness, and then slowly retracts its arm with a lingering sense of fatigue.
planning_shot:
Visualization: The robot raises its hand to one eye, lightly rubs it, and lowers away with a tired lingering finish.
Iconic pose: The hand clearly covering or touching one eye.
Recognition anchor: Direct placement at the eye region followed by small local rubbing.
Motion read: The viewer should read tiredness quickly from the eye-targeted reach and rub.
Pre-action reveal: Reach to the eye first before any rubbing begins.
Why this example matters: Tired fails when the motion becomes generic midair oscillation instead of a specific eye rub.

description: The robot first reveals a clean, slightly off-center 'face' presentation so the viewer can read the head area, then performs a cute side tilt that clearly favors one side, holds that tilted silhouette for a beat, and eases out with a tiny lingering inquisitive adjustment.
planning_shot:
Visualization: The robot looks like it notices something interesting, subtly presenting its face before tipping its 'head' to one side in a cute, readable way.
Iconic pose: A clearly side-tilted head-like silhouette, held for a beat.
Recognition anchor: The gripper/head region must visibly lean left or right, not just wobble generically.
Motion read: Within the first second, the viewer should read 'curious head tilt,' not just 'small movement.'
Pre-action reveal: Present the head area slightly forward and to one side before the tilt, so the tilt has a clear baseline.
Why this example matters: Curiosity fails when the tilt is too subtle or when the motion reads as generic fidgeting.

cue: Bow slightly from the waist (Respect / Greeting)
description: The robot settles into a modest chest-height stance, then performs a single coupled forward-and-downward bow, holds the respectful lowered line briefly, and rises back up without extra flourish.
planning_shot:
Visualization: The robot gives a restrained, polite bow with one clean dip and a readable hold at the lowest point.
Iconic pose: A visibly lowered respectful torso line, not just a generic forward pitch.
Recognition anchor: The bow should read as both forward and downward at the same time, so the arm silhouette clearly dips.
Motion read: The viewer should immediately read a polite bow rather than a loose shoulder swing.
Pre-action reveal: Establish a simple upright baseline pose before the coupled bow begins.
Why this example matters: Bow fails when only one axis changes and the motion reads like a generic pitch instead of a respectful dip.
